answer.rationale: Incumbent refusal plus a hard 18% spend cut and a 14-day non-auto-renewing primary contract leave renew/defer/second-source unable to both keep coverage and hit cost. The low-cost quote is the only path that meets the mandate; c2 is the supporting precedent (prior primary move, quick onboard, clean invoices) and must be checked before treating onboarding as safe. c1 is the counter-precedent: incumbent renewal avoided migration and delivery breaks, which matters at 94% utilization with no buffer—any slip is a line-down event that can dominate TCO. Lean switch to secure price and continuity of a contract, but flag downstream disruption risk and do not treat c2’s “quick” onboarding as proven for a no-buffer cutover until the archive is pulled.
